$comment: Vascula built-in filters (https://vascula.dev/filters) and Tringify platform filters (https://dev-docs.tringify.com/themes/platform-filters).

filters.name: upcase
filters.doc: Converts to upper case.
filters.example: {{ "Café au lait" | upcase }}  →  CAFÉ AU LAIT

filters.name: downcase
filters.doc: Converts to lower case.
filters.example: {{ "Café AU Lait" | downcase }}  →  café au lait

filters.name: capitalize
filters.doc: Upper-cases the first character and lower-cases the rest.
filters.example: {{ "éCLAIR WITH CREAM" | capitalize }}  →  Éclair with cream

filters.name: strip
filters.doc: Removes whitespace from both ends.

filters.name: lstrip
filters.doc: Removes whitespace from the start.

filters.name: rstrip
filters.doc: Removes whitespace from the end.

filters.name: strip_newlines
filters.doc: Removes every line break.

filters.name: append
filters.doc: Adds text at the end.

filters.name: prepend
filters.doc: Adds text at the start.

filters.name: replace
filters.doc: Replaces every occurrence of `old` with `new`.

filters.name: replace_first
filters.doc: Replaces the first occurrence of `old` with `new`.

filters.name: remove
filters.doc: Deletes every occurrence of the text.

filters.name: remove_first
filters.doc: Deletes the first occurrence of the text.

filters.name: truncate
filters.doc: Shortens text to at most `length` characters, counting the ending. The default length is 50 and the default ending is `...`. Text that already fits is unchanged; characters are never split.

filters.name: truncatewords
filters.doc: Keeps the first `count` words and adds the ending (default `...`) when it removed any. Runs of whitespace become single spaces. The count must be at least 1.
filters.example: {{ "one two  three four" | truncatewords: 2 }}  →  one two...

filters.name: split
filters.doc: Splits text into an array. An empty separator splits into single characters; an empty input gives an empty array.

filters.name: slice
filters.doc: Returns part of a string or an array. A negative offset counts from the end. The length defaults to 1.

filters.name: size
filters.doc: The number of characters in a string, items in an array, or keys in a map. Anything else is 0. The `.size` property gives the same result.

filters.name: escape
filters.doc: Escapes text for HTML. Printing the result does not escape it again, so `escape` never double-escapes. Output is escaped anyway; use it when you store markup-safe text in a variable or pass it to an application filter. Applications cannot replace this filter.

filters.name: escape_once
filters.doc: Escapes text that may already contain character references, without escaping them a second time.

filters.name: strip_html
filters.doc: Removes everything between `<` and `>`. The result is text and is escaped when printed. This is not a sanitizer: use it for plain-text summaries.

filters.name: newline_to_br
filters.doc:
Escapes the text and replaces each line break with `
`.

filters.name: plus
filters.doc: Adds. Two integers give an exact integer; anything with a decimal gives a decimal.

filters.name: minus
filters.doc: Subtracts. Two integers give an exact integer; anything with a decimal gives a decimal.

filters.name: times
filters.doc: Multiplies. Two integers give an exact integer; anything with a decimal gives a decimal.

filters.name: divided_by
filters.doc: Divides. Two integers that divide exactly give an integer; otherwise the result is a decimal. Dividing by zero is an error.

filters.name: modulo
filters.doc: The remainder of a division, exact for two integers. Its sign follows the input. A zero divisor is an error.

filters.name: round
filters.doc: Rounds to the nearest integer, or to `places` decimal places. Halves round away from zero.

filters.name: ceil
filters.doc: Rounds up, optionally keeping `places` decimal places.

filters.name: floor
filters.doc: Rounds down, optionally keeping `places` decimal places.

filters.name: abs
filters.doc: The absolute value.

filters.name: at_least
filters.doc: Returns the larger of the value and `n`.

filters.name: at_most
filters.doc: Returns the smaller of the value and `n`.

filters.name: join
filters.doc: Prints each item and joins them. The separator defaults to no separator.

filters.name: first
filters.doc: The first item, or `nil` for an empty array. The `.first` property does the same.

filters.name: last
filters.doc: The last item, or `nil` for an empty array. The `.last` property does the same.

filters.name: map
filters.doc: Returns an array of one field from each item.

filters.name: where
filters.doc: `where: field` keeps the items whose field is truthy; `where: field, value` keeps the items whose field equals the value.

filters.name: sort
filters.doc: Orders items ascending, or by a field. Numbers sort as numbers and strings in character order (upper case before lower case). Items that cannot be compared keep their original order.

filters.name: sort_natural
filters.doc: Orders items by their printed text, ignoring case.

filters.name: reverse
filters.doc: Reverses the order.

filters.name: uniq
filters.doc: Removes repeated items, keeping the first of each. Items compare with equality, so `1` and `1.0` are the same.

filters.name: compact
filters.doc: Removes `nil` items.

filters.name: concat
filters.doc: Joins two arrays.

filters.name: sum
filters.doc: Adds up the items, or one field of each item. Items that are not numbers are skipped.

filters.name: date
filters.doc: Formats a date with strftime directives (`%Y %m %d %e %B %b %A %a %H %I %p %M %S %j %s %Z %z %%`). The input is a date string, a date value, or `"now"` / `"today"` (UTC). A value that is not a date, or a missing format, is an error.

filters.name: url_encode
filters.doc: Encodes text for a URL query. Spaces become `+`.

filters.name: url_decode
filters.doc: Decodes URL query text.

filters.name: default
filters.doc: Returns the fallback when the value is `nil`, `false`, an empty string or an empty collection. `0` is a real value and is kept. With `allow_false: true`, an explicit `false` is kept. Applications cannot replace this filter.

filters.name: json
filters.doc: Converts a value to JSON. Inside `<script>` it is printed with `<`, `>` and `&` encoded; inside an HTML tag it is also escaped for HTML. Map keys are written in sorted order. Applications cannot replace this filter.

filters.name: money
filters.doc: Formats a price in the shopper's language, in the price's own currency (`₹1,234.56` in English, `1 234,56 ₹` in French). Use a price value such as `product.price.current`, not a plain number. `isolate: true` keeps the price together inside text written in the other direction.

filters.name: t
filters.doc: Prints the text for a key from the theme's `locales/<locale>.json` in the shopper's language, falling back to the theme's default language. Named arguments fill `{{ placeholder }}` slots. A missing key prints `translation missing: <locale>.<key>`.

filters.name: image_url
filters.doc: Gives the URL of a store image resized to the width you ask for, rounded up to 160, 320, 480, 640, 828, 1080, 1440 or 2048 pixels. The input is an image object, an image setting or a store image URL. An empty input gives an empty string.

filters.name: image_srcset
filters.doc: Lists the image at every width up to `max` (2048 if not given), for the browser to choose from.

filters.name: image_loading
filters.doc: Prints the loading attributes for an image: the first image on the page loads first, the next two load straight away, and the rest load as they scroll into view.

filters.name: asset_url
filters.doc: Gives the URL of a file in the theme's `assets/` folder: fonts (`.woff2`, `.woff`) and images (`.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.webp`, `.gif`). An unknown file name is an error.

filters.name: placeholder_svg
filters.doc: Prints artwork for a slot the merchant has not filled yet: `image`, `logo`, `product-1`…`product-6`, `collection-1`…`collection-6`, `lifestyle-1`, `lifestyle-2`.

filters.name: placeholder_video
filters.doc: Gives the URL of a placeholder video: `reel-1`, `reel-2`, `reel-3` or `reel-4`.
